Social Stratification

Social stratification — caste, class, gender and inequality — and how they affect access to health care.

🎯 After this chapter you can

  • Define social stratification
  • Describe caste and class in India
  • Explain how stratification affects health care access

In simple words

Social stratification is the division of society into layers or strata based on caste, class, gender, race or religion. People in higher strata usually have more money, power and access to health care.

Stratification is unequal and often passes from one generation to the next. It creates differences in health and life expectancy.

Forms of stratification

Form Basis Indian example
Caste Birth Brahmin, Dalit, tribal groups
Class Wealth, occupation, education Rich, middle class, poor
Gender Male, female, third gender Men, women, transgender persons
Race Physical features Less common in India

Inequality and health

  • Lower strata often live in crowded, unsanitary conditions.
  • They may not afford treatment or medicines.
  • They may face disrespect in health facilities.
  • Women and girls often eat last and get less care.

Social mobility

Social mobility is movement between strata — up or down. Education and jobs are the main routes upward in India.

🔴 Health inequality

People in lower strata get less health care and have worse health. Nurses should give equal care to all and notice financial barriers.

Where the nurse uses this

  • Notice cost barriers — a patient may skip medicines because of price; suggest cheaper options or schemes.
  • Treat all equally — give the same respect and care to every patient regardless of caste, class or gender.
  • Respect dignity — do not make assumptions based on how a patient dresses or speaks.
  • Report discrimination — if a patient is treated unfairly, tell the senior nurse or doctor.
  • Use government schemes — help eligible patients access free or low-cost care.

🔴 Most important for exams

  1. Social stratification is the division of society into unequal layers.
  2. Forms include caste, class, gender and religion.
  3. Lower strata have less money, power and health-care access.
  4. Caste is by birth; class is based on wealth, occupation and education.
  5. Stratification causes health inequality.

⭐ Important for exams

  1. Social mobility is movement up or down between strata.
  2. Education and jobs are common routes upward in India.
  3. Women and girls often receive less food and care within families.

📌 Memory trick

Stratification bases: “C-C-G-R” — Caste, Class, Gender, Religion.

60-second revision

  • Stratification = division into unequal layers.
  • Bases: caste, class, gender, religion.
  • Lower strata = less access to health care.
  • Caste by birth; class by wealth/education/occupation.
  • Nurses give equal care and notice cost barriers.

Test yourself

Social stratification means:

Answer: B. Stratification is the division of society into ranked, unequal layers.

Caste is based on:

Answer: B. Caste is ascribed by birth and usually lasts a lifetime.

Which group usually has worse access to health care?

Answer: B. Lower strata have less money and power and face more barriers to care.

Social mobility means:

Answer: B. Social mobility is movement between social strata, usually through education or jobs.

A nurse should treat patients:

Answer: B. Nurses must give equal respect and care to every patient, whatever their social position.
